description:
Located in the historical center, the B&B is situated in an ancient building which was part, already in 1300, of a Franciscan convent.
From the terrace where in the summer breakfast is served you can enjoy the peace of the ancient garden.
neighborhood_overview:
The house is adjacent the Garden of the Abbey, one of the quietest and most striking of Venice.
The very near street "Fondamenta della Misericordia" is well known in town for the numerous places where is possible to appreciate Venetian or ethnic specialities, and listen to music in the evening. Not far you can find the ancient Jewish Ghetto with its seven synagogues, the Church of "Madonna dell’Orto" and "Ca’ d’Oro"!
host_about:
I'am Marco, I'm Venetian. I left Venice in 1999 to work in Rome and then in Milan where I met Alessandra.
Alessandra was born and lived all her life  in Milan, where she studied (high school of arts) and she worked in an advertising agency.
It’s in In Milan where our  love story began and in milan our daughter Anita was born.
After having lived the reality of these two big italian metropolis, we have decided to give  Anita the opportunity to grow up in Venice.
I take care of everything related to the B & B and Alessandra follows the house chores and Anita.
Being in Venice, in this lagoon -  apart from  the cultural feedbacks which  are unique to  this  place -  you have  the chance to rediscover the "the natural passing of time" of the elements like water and earth (one almost always walks  ... or uses the boat ) and also helps you to rediscover the "more personal and intimate time". So, at least, it has  always been for me, every time I  come back to this town.
The area in  which we live , is a little secluded and still lived  by Venetians, with its historical places: the "Bacari" and its taverns, its silences and the spoken dialect, which  induces you to enjoy authentically the ancient dimension of a ‘water town’. Moreover, the house we have chosen,is luminous and surrounded by the green of an ex Franciscan cloister which encourages you to rediscover your more relaxed inner condition.
In  this house we have started  again to practise Yoga, as we were doing before our busy days at work and the birth of  Anita.
We sincerely hope that the guests who will come to visit us, besides to appreciate the city’s beauty and its history, may  also enjoy this more intimate experience and that they will  keep  the memory on  their return back home.
See you soon. Marco

You will be tucked away from the crowds in a tranquil corner watching gondolas float past your windows. You can also take folding chairs or cushions and sit out by the canal landing outside the front door. neighborhood_overview:
Dorsoduro is one of six sestieri or districts of central Venice and is located on the south-western side of town. It includes the long, southern shore of the city which faces over the water to the Giudecca.

Dorsoduro is our favourite district of Venice. It houses some of the city's finest art, best museums, most picturesque canals and palazzi, not to mention some of the coolest cafes and most stylish restaurants in town. This vibrant, bohemian area is home to Venice's university, ensuring the general vibe is artistic, youthful and relaxed.

Dorsoduro's eastern end stretches out to the panoramic Punto della Dogana, which has recently reopened as a fantastic new exhibition space. At this end of the sestiere you'll find grand palazzi and, at the Accademia Bridge, the most attractive stretch of the Grand Canal.

host_about:
For your Holidays without troubles!! Let me introduce myself. I’m Manuela, I’m 35 years old and I was born in Venice. I love my city, I consider it unique but I know like every major tourist destination, Venice has two different faces. There’s the Venice of the tourists, made of predictable routes and their restaurants, created for those who are just passing by and probably are not coming back twice. You spend hours queued just to visit the most famous churches or museums. That’s the chaotic Venice, with a lot of unfamiliar faces that don’t give help when you need it. And then there is the Venice of the Venetians, where everybody knows each other. That’s the Venice with secret restaurants, bars and cicchetterie (typical Venetian local) where you can eat divinely without spending too much, places frequented by people who charachterise and make the city unique. That’s not the touristic Venice: even those who are visiting the city for the first time, can feel its real soul. And this is the Venice I’d like people to know, even if for just a few days. 
Therefore, if you don’t like the “tourist trap” city but you want to see its real soul, let me host you in my house. By booking a stay at Venetian MOOD, you won’t only choose a place to sleep, but you will be greeted by friends you can count on, in order to live your experience in Venice in the best way! Carefree, without stress or last minute bad surprises. If you’re looking to be a tourist in Venice, to eat in expensive low level restaurants and bars, to get carried away by the routes designed for tourists regardless of who they are, I respect that, but you might prefer another housing.

Marghera is a venetian city borough located in the area of Terraferma, and should not be confused with ‘Porto Marghera’ which refers to the port and former chemical industrial area of Venice.

Before the port and residential areas were built, Marghera was mainly a swamp land known as Bottenighi, where the few roads occasionally disappeared under the shifting shoals of thick sand. The current day 'Via F.lli Bandiera' was once a long drainage canal that ran down from the 'Malcontenta', a palladian villa. It was part of a 14th century hydraulic system built in order to collect the water that flows from Terraferma, and thus diverting it away from Venice.

name: A COZY PLACE IN THE HEART OF VENICE
host_about:
ENGLISH:
I am from Tuscany, but have lived in Venice for many years. After studying languages and Oriental literature in Venice, I travelled and lived abroad for many years. On my return to Italy in 2001 I decided to move to Venice, simply bewitched by the indescribable beauty of this city. For the past 10 years I have been managing a bookshop, a marvellous job, however, I have now decided to take a sabbatical year to develop new projects. 
Up until a year ago I was living with my husband and son in the apartment that I am now letting; we still like it a lot since it's where we passed many happy and important years. 
We moved to another apartment due to a need of more space and so, loving the area, we now live only 5 minutes away from our old house.
The area  is truly one of the best in Venice; here you can still find genuine Venetian life, full of vitality. Venice is a unique city that deserves time and respect. It is well worth exploring off the usual tourist trail...try loosing yourself in the labyrinth of hiidden 'calli' (Venetian streets); perhaps stopping at a small typical local bar to drink a glass of wine - 'un'ombra' and eat a 'cicchetto' and other Venetian specialities. 
We are happy to advise you on all aspects of local life as well as the highlights and to be of assistance in any way we can to make your stay in Venice an enjoyable one.

ITALIANO:
Sono una toscana trapiantata a Venezia da molti anni ormai. Dopo aver studiato qui Lingue e Letterature Orientali ho viaggiato e vissuto diversi anni all'estero ma, nel 2001, al mio ritorno in Italia ho deciso di tornare, stregata dalla bellezza inesplicabile di questa città. Negli ultimi dieci anni ho fatto la libraia, un mestiere meraviglioso, e adesso ho deciso di prendermi una anno sabbatico per meditare nuovi progetti. 
L'appartamento che affitto è quello dove vivevo con mio marito e mio figlio fino ad un anno fa, noi lo amiamo ancora molto, ci abbiamo passato anni felici ed importanti. La zona è una delle migliori rimaste a Venezia, dove ancora esiste una vivace vita di quartiere animata da veri veneziani. Per questo, pur avendo traslocato per necessità di spazio (nel frattempo la famiglia si è allargata a quattro gatti e un cane), siamo rimasti nello stesso quartiere, a cinque minuti dalla vecchia casa. 
Questa è una città unica, che va rispettata e che val la pena assaporare cercando di uscire dai soliti flussi turistici per perdersi nelle calli "sconte" e ritrovarsi a bere un'ombra e mangiare un cicchetto nascosti in un piccolo bacaro di quartiere. In questo ed altro vi posso aiutare :)

name: Ca' Canaletto Canal View Refreshed in 2024!
description:
Refreshed in 2024!

In an enchanting location overlooking one of the prettiest canals in all of Venice, a bright and classic two bedroom apartment situated in a tranquil position right next door to the Convent of the Eremite – the perfect Venetian experience.
neighborhood_overview:
Peaceful, though certainly not isolated, the apartment is but a minute’s walk from the gentle activities of a thriving neighbourhood - take a short stroll down the alleyway opposite, with its little illuminated shrine and enticing air of secrecy, before suddenly arriving onto the Fondamenta Toletta, a charming street of bookshops, bar, gelataria, ATM and the canalside tables of the small, but highly popular, ‘Enoteca Ai Artisti’.

Also within a minute of the fine restaurants of Calle Lunga San Barnaba which leads directly to the delightful Campo San Barnaba and then onto the Ca’ Rezzonico vaporetto stop and the highly impressive Ca’ Rezzonico Museum of 18th Century Art, with its commemorative plaque to the poet Robert Browning, directly shouldering the Grand Canal.

Perfect location: quiet but central, very typical area, close to waterbus stop Giardini and Via Garibaldi (main street: supermarket, market, restaurants, cafés, banks, post office, chemist's, etc.), beside Biennale and within walking distance to St Mark's Square.

The apartment is made of 2 bedrooms, living room kitchenette and bathroom.

neighborhood_overview:
The flat is located in one of the more typical and unchanged areas of Venice, within easy walking distance of St. Mark’s Square and only a few steps from the main exhibition centre of "La Biennale".

From the nearby canal side you will be able to enjoy an enchanting view of St. Mark’s Square (really unforgettable during the sunset!).

Nearby there are numerous restaurants where you can enjoy traditional dishes, pizzerias, bars, supermarkets, baker's and chemist's shops, banks and much more besides.

The flat is near the "Giardini" and "Arsenale" water bus stops and is therefore easy to reach whether you arrive by car, train or plane (direct connection from airport).

The "Giardini" and "Arsenale" stops are served by all the main public transport lines (1 – 4.1– 4.2 – 5.1 – 5.2 – 6). From the flat, you can therefore easily reach any part of the city and its splendid islands (Lido, Murano, Burano, Torcello, etc).

description:

neighborhood_overview:
Cannaregio it is the largest, lively and populated quarter of the city, it takes the whole northern part of the city, it is delimited by the Lagoon, the Grand Canal and the Castello and Saint Mark Sestiere. The Cannaregio canal is the most important water way of the quarter right after the Grand Canal and it is the only inner canal crossed by the ACTV (public transport company) boats. Also Cannaregio is linked to the mainland by a bridge, it is the long railroad bridge from the Santa Lucia Train station to the mainland.
Its name come probably by the fact that here there where many reed thicket. This appear also on a book date 1410. This is a popular quarter of Venice, well know for the presence of the Jewish getto (the oldest in Europe).

host_about:
Sono Silvia, property manager e titolare dell’agenzia Immobiliare Veneziacentopercento, specializzata in ambito turistico nel centro storico di Venezia. 
Sono appassionata di arte, musica e Venezia, dove sono nata dove ho sempre vissuto. 
Nel 1995 ho unito i miei interessi per creare e costruire la mia attività, con l’obbiettivo di condividere con quante più persone possibile l'atmosfera di una città speciale e unica, diversa da qualsiasi altra  al mondo, facendola conoscere e amare nei suoi aspetti più intimi.
Ho iniziato con una sola stanza, a Casa mia, che ancora oggi è un B&B, fino a gestire oltre 20 diverse strutture per conto terzi.
Ho scelto di concentrarmi nel Sestiere di Castello, fulcro dell'antica Serenissima, perché qui è ancora possibile apprezzare appieno la più autentica quotidianità veneziana.
Per me e il mio staff la priorità assoluta è aiutare gli ospiti a vivere un’esperienza “al cento per cento”, cercando di trasformare i semplici turisti in viaggiatori consapevoli, “veneziani temporanei”, trasmettendo loro la passione per Venezia e il suo ambiente complesso e delicato, dove acqua e terra si sono unite come in una magia.

Ca' San Trovaso guesthouse is located in the centre of Venice, close to Accademia bridge, on Rio delle Romite in the heart of Dorsoduro, one of the most traditional and exclusive residential areas in Venice.

Our comfortable rooms and attentive family management, similar to that of a B&B, will make you feel at home, helping you to get to know the city also through the eyes of its residents so that you have the possibility to live the city authentically. A lovely continental breakfast, served in your room, is included in the price.

The other square is mpty and quiet, opening onto Venice's most beautiful canals (Ognissanti, Romite)—a painter’s paradise.

Most of the local bars and pastry shops on the San Trovaso Canal and Calle della Toletta are frequented by the locals who meet for an afternoon drink or by tourists who have come to admire one of the only four squeros (gondola boatyards) still operating in Venice, and the only one that has kept its traditional look.

The Gallerie dell'Accademia is only a stone's throw away, while the Piazza San Marco is only a 15-minute walk away.

description: This romantic apartment is located in the heart of the Castello district, an area where you can still breathe the air of the most authentic Venice. neighborhood_overview: Castello is one of the most authentic "sestieri" of Venice as it is mostly inhabited by residents. Piazza San Marco can be reached in 12 minutes on foot, while the Biennale Gardens are just 5 minutes away on foot. At the "Giardini" stop, 5 vaporetto lines pass, including those for the station and the airport. Two stops away is the Venice Lido, which hosts the famous Film Festival. If you want to enjoy a spritz with "cicchetti", a typical Venetian aperitif, take the historic via Garibaldi, full of life and services, full of small restaurants and "bacari" and, perhaps, go inside until you find the fruit boat docked on the canal , where you can buy the unobtainable grapes of Sant'Erasmo, an agricultural island in the lagoon. Every corner of this district will reserve you a surprise: like having breakfast in the ancient greenhouses of Venice, or strolling in the Napoleonic gardens and in the tree-lined avenues of what can be defined as the green soul of the city.

neighborhood_overview:
Lovely and spacious studio apartment with a picturesque view of the Canal dei Vetrai; situated on the main artery of the island of Murano.
As one meanders through Murano, up and down the fondamenta, over bridges, and in and out of glass stores, one can readily appreciate delicate reproductions of period pieces as well as colorful modern pieces from the island’s most prestigious glass factories and famous contemporary artists.
One can as well visit the many glass factories and watch the art of glass making. Entrance is free, and there are assigned people who speak different languages that will explain the process.
Along the way, one can find several typical outside restaurants where one can savor the specialties of the Lagoon such as fish, various delicious pasta, pizza,and many other traditional local and regional dishes.

name: Venice with great terrace, Castello
description: Venice Riva 7 Martiri, 70 sqm apartment with terrace, sleeps up to 4 minimum three nights
neighborhood_overview:
Castello is the largest of the six sestieri of Venice, Italy. The district grew up from the thirteenth century around a naval dockyard on what was originally the Isole Gemini, although there had been small settlements of the islands of San Pietro di Castello (for which the sestiere is named), also called Isola d'Olivolo, since at least the eighth century.
The district became divided between the Arsenale, then the largest naval complex in Europe, and the monasteries in the north of the quarter. It was later altered by Napoleon, who planned what are now the Bienniale Gardens, and still more recently the island of Sant'Elena has been created, and land drained at other extremities of the quarter.
Other attractions in Castello include the Scuola di San Marco, the Church of Santi Giovanni e Paolo, the Scuola of San Giorgio degli Schiavoni, the church of San Giorgio dei Greci, the Campo Santa Maria Formosa, the Church of La Pietà and the Church of San Zaccaria.

host_about:
I'am Marco, I'm Venetian. I left Venice in 1999 to work in Rome and then in Milan where I met Alessandra.
Alessandra was born and lived all her life  in Milan, where she studied (high school of arts) and she worked in an advertising agency.
It’s in In Milan where our  love story began and in milan our daughter Anita was born.
After having lived the reality of these two big italian metropolis, we have decided to give  Anita the opportunity to grow up in Venice.
I take care of everything related to the B & B and Alessandra follows the house chores and Anita.
Being in Venice, in this lagoon -  apart from  the cultural feedbacks which  are unique to  this  place -  you have  the chance to rediscover the "the natural passing of time" of the elements like water and earth (one almost always walks  ... or uses the boat ) and also helps you to rediscover the "more personal and intimate time". So, at least, it has  always been for me, every time I  come back to this town.
The area in  which we live , is a little secluded and still lived  by Venetians, with its historical places: the "Bacari" and its taverns, its silences and the spoken dialect, which  induces you to enjoy authentically the ancient dimension of a ‘water town’. Moreover, the house we have chosen,is luminous and surrounded by the green of an ex Franciscan cloister which encourages you to rediscover your more relaxed inner condition.
In  this house we have started  again to practise Yoga, as we were doing before our busy days at work and the birth of  Anita.
We sincerely hope that the guests who will come to visit us, besides to appreciate the city’s beauty and its history, may  also enjoy this more intimate experience and that they will  keep  the memory on  their return back home.
See you soon. Marco

Calle de la Madona is in a traditional, tranquil part of the Dorsoduro in a sleepy corner of Venice. The population comprises students from the Architecture College, local Venetian families and boatmen. As a consequence the area is authentically Venetian, safe, restful – and much cheaper than the rest of the city!

There are some astonishing churches within walking distance:
San Nicolo dei Mendicoli, Angelo Raffaele, The Carmini, San Pantalon, San Sebastiano, Scuola Grande di San Rocco and The Frari.

Campo Santa Margherita: This is the Bohemian, social hub of the Dorsoduro (6 min walk), with late-night bars, restaurants, clubs, cafés, ice-cream parlours, pizza shops, supermarkets, hardware shops, pharmacies etc. It is vibrant and lively. Good for evening ice-cream and last drink before bed.

Restaurants and bars: ‘La Bifora’ (Salamis, parma ham, cheeses, nibbles etc), ‘Dallo Zio’ (Pasta and traditional Venetian food at reasonable prices), ‘Chet Bar’
host_about:
My Profile:
My name is Gerard and I bought this house in 2013 . I am from the UK and am an art historian, writer and artist. I taught the history of painting, sculpture and architecture for thirty years and decided that was quite enough. The Italian Renaissance was my specialty – so the idea of buying a house in one of the historical, cultural capitals of the world was not a difficult decision to make. I love the opera and classical music and Venice is full of both. My favourite things to do here are to run in the early morning, (before the tourists are up) and wander the streets in the late evening, (when the tourists are in bed). I try really hard to get lost when I’m out walking and consciously take wrong turnings to see where I end up. It’s the best way to discover the city. My golden rule is never to pass a church if the door is open; there is always some new painting or sculpture to discover inside.

neighborhood_overview: Try to avoid high summer months, but whatever time of year you go, don’t try to see Venice all in a day. neighborhood_overview:
YOU WILL NOT FIND HIGH TIDE IN VENICE
High tide is a phenomenon that occurs almost exclusively in November and December, and can reach potentially wet levels around 4 times a year, for a few hours a day.


It DOES NOT LAST LONG TIME
The high tide lasts 3-4 hours and affects only the lower areas of the city. An exceptional tide can occur, statistically, once every 5 years.

BEWARE OF FAKE NEWS
Global Media have reported catastrophically the high tide of November 2019. The truth is, Venice has coexisted for centuries with this recurring phenomenon, which on this very rare occasion reached maximum levels out of the ordinary for a few hours.

DO AS THE LOCALS DO
Venice is a very lively city, even during the high tide hours. On these rare occasions, you will need just a pair of high boots to enjoy the city and its attractions as the locals do!

neighborhood_overview:
DORSODURO DISTRICT
The Sestiere of Dorsoduro got its name form the characteristic morphology of the island were it was built, this side of the city was less swampy and had an harder surface, in Venetian Dorso duro (hard back).
At the moment it counts about 15.000 inhabitants including also Giudecca and Sacca Fisola island (both part of the quarter).
It is partially washed by the Canal Grande and Canale della Giudecca and border with San Polo sestiere and Santa Croce, it is linked with Saint Mark’ s quarter by the Accademia Bridge.
Its history had begun by the Mendrigola island and it is even older than Rialto one, all other islands composing the quarter were colonized successively and arrives until Punta della Dogana (once the customs of the city).
This Sestiere is rich of churches and museums as well the Ca’ Foscari university main site. It’s a quite lively and popular quarter, where the streets of tourists and Venetians cross each other in perfect harmony.

host_about:
For your Holidays without troubles!! Let me introduce myself. I’m Manuela, I’m 35 years old and I was born in Venice. I love my city, I consider it unique but I know like every major tourist destination, Venice has two different faces. There’s the Venice of the tourists, made of predictable routes and their restaurants, created for those who are just passing by and probably are not coming back twice. You spend hours queued just to visit the most famous churches or museums. That’s the chaotic Venice, with a lot of unfamiliar faces that don’t give help when you need it. And then there is the Venice of the Venetians, where everybody knows each other. That’s the Venice with secret restaurants, bars and cicchetterie (typical Venetian local) where you can eat divinely without spending too much, places frequented by people who charachterise and make the city unique. That’s not the touristic Venice: even those who are visiting the city for the first time, can feel its real soul. And this is the Venice I’d like people to know, even if for just a few days. 
Therefore, if you don’t like the “tourist trap” city but you want to see its real soul, let me host you in my house. By booking a stay at Venetian MOOD, you won’t only choose a place to sleep, but you will be greeted by friends you can count on, in order to live your experience in Venice in the best way! Carefree, without stress or last minute bad surprises. If you’re looking to be a tourist in Venice, to eat in expensive low level restaurants and bars, to get carried away by the routes designed for tourists regardless of who they are, I respect that, but you might prefer another housing.

For your Holidays without troubles!! Let me introduce myself. I’m Manuela, I’m 35 years old and I was born in Venice. I love my city, I consider it unique but I know like every major tourist destination, Venice has two different faces. There’s the Venice of the tourists, made of predictable routes and their restaurants, created for those who are just passing by and probably are not coming back twice. You spend hours queued just to visit the most famous churches or museums. That’s the chaotic Venice, with a lot of unfamiliar faces that don’t give help when you need it. And then there is the Venice of the Venetians, where everybody knows each other. That’s the Venice with secret restaurants, bars and cicchetterie (typical Venetian local) where you can eat divinely without spending too much, places frequented by people who charachterise and make the city unique. That’s not the touristic Venice: even those who are visiting the city for the first time, can feel its real soul. And this is the Venice I’d like people to know, even if for just a few days. 
Therefore, if you don’t like the “tourist trap” city but you want to see its real soul, let me host you in my house. By booking a stay at Venetian MOOD, you won’t only choose a place to sleep, but you will be greeted by friends you can count on, in order to live your experience in Venice in the best way! Carefree, without stress or last minute bad surprises. If you’re looking to be a tourist in Venice, to eat in expensive low level restaurants and bars, to get carried away by the routes designed for tourists regardless of who they are, I respect that, but you might prefer another housing.

For your Holidays without troubles!! Let me introduce myself. I’m Manuela, I’m 35 years old and I was born in Venice. I love my city, I consider it unique but I know like every major tourist destination, Venice has two different faces. There’s the Venice of the tourists, made of predictable routes and their restaurants, created for those who are just passing by and probably are not coming back twice. You spend hours queued just to visit the most famous churches or museums. That’s the chaotic Venice, with a lot of unfamiliar faces that don’t give help when you need it. And then there is the Venice of the Venetians, where everybody knows each other. That’s the Venice with secret restaurants, bars and cicchetterie (typical Venetian local) where you can eat divinely without spending too much, places frequented by people who charachterise and make the city unique. That’s not the touristic Venice: even those who are visiting the city for the first time, can feel its real soul. And this is the Venice I’d like people to know, even if for just a few days. 
Therefore, if you don’t like the “tourist trap” city but you want to see its real soul, let me host you in my house. By booking a stay at Venetian MOOD, you won’t only choose a place to sleep, but you will be greeted by friends you can count on, in order to live your experience in Venice in the best way! Carefree, without stress or last minute bad surprises. If you’re looking to be a tourist in Venice, to eat in expensive low level restaurants and bars, to get carried away by the routes designed for tourists regardless of who they are, I respect that, but you might prefer another housing.

The heart of the sestiere is certainly Piazza San Marco, known as the "living room of the world" because it is the seat of the most important political and religious events for the Republic of Venice, as well as the center of all Venetian life for about a millennium. host_about:
For your Holidays without troubles!! Let me introduce myself. I’m Manuela, I’m 35 years old and I was born in Venice. I love my city, I consider it unique but I know like every major tourist destination, Venice has two different faces. There’s the Venice of the tourists, made of predictable routes and their restaurants, created for those who are just passing by and probably are not coming back twice. You spend hours queued just to visit the most famous churches or museums. That’s the chaotic Venice, with a lot of unfamiliar faces that don’t give help when you need it. And then there is the Venice of the Venetians, where everybody knows each other. That’s the Venice with secret restaurants, bars and cicchetterie (typical Venetian local) where you can eat divinely without spending too much, places frequented by people who charachterise and make the city unique. That’s not the touristic Venice: even those who are visiting the city for the first time, can feel its real soul. And this is the Venice I’d like people to know, even if for just a few days. 
Therefore, if you don’t like the “tourist trap” city but you want to see its real soul, let me host you in my house. By booking a stay at Venetian MOOD, you won’t only choose a place to sleep, but you will be greeted by friends you can count on, in order to live your experience in Venice in the best way! Carefree, without stress or last minute bad surprises. If you’re looking to be a tourist in Venice, to eat in expensive low level restaurants and bars, to get carried away by the routes designed for tourists regardless of who they are, I respect that, but you might prefer another housing.

neighborhood_overview:
Castello is the largest of the six sestieri of Venice, Italy.
There had been, since at least the 8th-century, small settlements of the islands of San Pietro di Castello (for which the sestiere is named). This island was also called Isola d'Olivolo.

From the thirteenth century onward, the district grew around a naval dockyard on what was originally the Isole Gemini. The land in the district was dominated by the Arsenale of the Republic of Venice, then the largest naval complex in Europe.

Other significant structures were by the monasteries in the north of the quarter.

Napoleon closed the Arsenal and planned what are now the Bienniale Gardens. More recently the island of Sant'Elena has been created, and more land drained at other extremities of Castello.

Prominent sites and buildings in Castello include:

Church of Santi Giovanni e Paolo (San Zanipoli)
Church of San Giorgio dei Greci
Campo Santa Maria Formosa and Church

description:
The house consists of a double bedroom and a comfortable double bedroom (or even double), large living room and kitchen equipped with everything you need to ensure a relaxing stay in a modern, functional environment.
Located in the well-known residential neighborhood of Sant'Elena surrounded by green areas, playground and great restaurants. Bright and cozy, the apartment is a 2-minute walk from the Giardini della Biennale entrance and 10 minutes from the Arsenal. Great for families and friends.
neighborhood_overview:
It is a very green and populated Venice, quiet and lively at the same time, that of S.Elena and S.Pietro di Castello.
Disembarking from the vaporetto to the S.Elena stop, from the Rimembranze park and from the public gardens, the view of the lagoon and the St. Mark's basin is splendid.
The whole area offers glimpses of hardworking and cheerful daily life, genuinely Venetian scenes not contaminated by the tourist influx, which is very scarce here.
In the extreme outskirts of the Castello district, the colors of the cloths between each house create light games in the canals, and the market on boats in the river of S. Anna finds an ideal continuation in the active shopping area of Venice's only street, Via Garibaldi.

... Via Garibaldi ...

This wide and crowded street was created by Napoleon in 1808 filling a canal.
Giovanni Caboto and his son Sebastiano lived there, the navigators who in 1497 arrived on what they believed to be from China.

name: Gheto Novo
description: The apartment is situated in the historical Jewish Ghetto of Venice, precisely in the Gheto Novo (New Gheto), which is, despite the misleading name, the oldest part of ghetto. The apartment is full of light, in spite of the low ceiling typical of the unique medieval “skyscrapers”(medieval buildings teeter up to six stories). The large canal, surrounding the island of the Gheto Novo, is visible from all the windows of the apartment. The building is adjacent to the Jewish Museum and to 3 synagogs
neighborhood_overview:
The Ghetto of Venice is the world's first ghetto; it was the walled quarter Venice created for its Jews in the 16th century.
The ghetto remains the focal point of Jewish life in Venice, with two operating synagogues, a Jewish library, day school, kosher food shops, a Jewish bakery. There's also the Jewish Museum, with a collection of 16th– to 19th-century artifacts. The museum offers guided tours of the neighborhood and several of its synagogues.
If Your stay occurs during a jewish festivity, You will have the unique possibility of observing the religious rites and listening to the chants of the orthodox Jews.

Campo San Polo is the largest open air public square in Venice, second only to Piazza San Marco. While originally a grazing area and pasture, it was paved in 1493. The water well in the center of the square is one of the last remaining wells in Venice. Campo San Polo was used for bullfights, mass sermons and masked balls. In 1549 Lorenzino de'Medici was assassinated here.
Attractions in the San Polo neighbourhood include: the Rialto Bridge, the Church of San Giacomo of Rialto. Only 10 minute walk to the Rialto Market vegetable and fish market (established in the year 1097). The vegetable market is open in the mornings Monday-Saturday, the seafood market is open Tuesday-Saturday mornings. Other attractions include the House of Goldoni, the Frari Church, the Church of San Rocco and the Scuola Grande di San Rocco.

description:
Live the charm of yesteryear in a romantic guest room in an authentic Venetian residence. Nestled on the second floor of a 1890 Muranese house, this private suite is a time capsule blending vintage and contemporary elements.

Featuring a queen-size bed, the en-suite bathroom with a shower is encased in glass walls, providing a scenic view. Ideal for a couple's retreat in an unconventional Venetian setting, close to the historic city center. Conveniently positioned in front of a water-bus stop.
neighborhood_overview:
Murano is very well-connected to all Venice key places, also during the night, but still blissfully off the beaten tracks of tourists.
The area is famous all over the world for glassblowing techniques: you will be able to witness artistry in action at the glass showrooms and furnaces scattered all over the island and at walking distance from the house.
A bridge away is the Glass Museum and the main church of St. Donato with 12th century gilded apse mosaic and a Byzantine style mosaic floor.

name: Two balconies with canal views
description:
The apartment is located in the district of CANNAREGIO, one of the most typical and romantic in Venice: it is a meeting place between inhabitants and tourists.
Strategically located: halfway between Piazzale Roma (car and bus terminal) - Railway station, and St. Mark's Square, all reachable on foot in 15 minutes
The house has been restored, consists of three bedrooms and two bathrooms, and two balconies with romantic view of the canal and foundation
Supermarkets, restaurants and bars nearby
Code Reg. 027042-LOC-05983
neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is in the center of the CANNAREGIO district.
The CANNAREGIO district is in a strategic position, being halfway between the points of arrival in Venice, Piazzale Roma (terminal for cars and buses) and train station of S. Lucia, and Piazza San Marco, all reachable on foot in 15 minutes from the apartment
CANNAREGIO is one of the most romantic, lively and authentic neighborhoods of Venice, inhabited by the several Venetians who reside here, and frequented by tourists who visit the various tourist attractions that there are. To name just a few: Ca 'd' Oro, Chiesa di Madonna dell 'Orto, Chiesa dei Miracoli, Jewish Ghetto, etc.
In the immediate vicinity of the apartment there are several supermarkets (where there are also foods already cooked, ready to eat), numerous bars (where you can taste the typical Venetian "cicchetti"), and many restaurants where you can taste Venetian specialties.
host_about:
Sono di origine veneziana.  Ho abitato fuori Venezia, anche per motivi di studio, ma da oltre 20 anni sono tornato a vivere nella meravigliosa e unica Venezia.
Laureato in matematica, attualmente amministro gli immobili di famiglia.
Amante della montagna, in particolare delle vicine Dolomiti, quando posso vado in montagna, per fare lunghe sciate in inverno, e qualche giro in bicicletta quando la neve è... finita.
Quando ho tempo "curo", mantengo, e "porto a spasso" la mia vecchia auto: una Lancia, naturalmente ! 
Adoro gli animali, specie i gatti e i cani; attualmente, però, non ho nessun "amico a quattro zampe".
Mi piacciono la natura, le piante e i fiori, che purtroppo qui a Venezia non sono troppo diffusi (come un po' in tutti i centri storici delle città).
Trovo molto interessante visitare i vecchi paesi e borghi, ed ammirare le vecchie costruzioni: per intuire gli antichi modi di vivere, le tradizioni, e le antiche tecniche di costruzione.
Mi piace seguire le commedie a teatro, e i vecchi film comici o gialli.
Riguardo alla cucina, mi piacciono le specialità venete in genere, e quelle toscane ed emiliane. Non disdegno altre specialità italiane o straniere, purché senza - o con poco - formaggio !

host_about:
Sono nata e cresciuta a Venezia. Di questa città amo la sua dimensione speciale e il fatto che sia un luogo multiculturale, pieno di arte, storia e bellezza e immerso in un contesto naturale fra acqua e cielo. Cerco di infondere questo amore per la mia città ai miei ospiti. Mi piace raccontare lo stile di vita di questa piccola isola non facile da girare. In certe stagioni può accadere di essere sopraffatti dal caldo, dalla folla di un turismo mal gestito, dai locandieri poco affabili. Per questo penso che il contatto con le persone del luogo sia fondamentale per poter meglio apprezzare l'animo vero di questa nostra Venezia. Soprattutto vi consiglierò un milione di posti dove mangiare e ben bere, è sempre un buon modo per conoscere l'Italia! 
Mi piace poter parlare le lingue dei miei ospiti e conoscere persone da tutto il mondo. Parlo inglese, francese, spagnolo e mi sto cimentando nello studio del russo. Sono appassionata di grammatica e lingue, infatti fra le mie attività c'è anche l'insegnamento dell'italiano per stranieri. Mi piace viaggiare, mi piace studiare in generale: mi appassiona la fotografia, arte che coltivo, il cinema, la letteratura, la storia, la politica e la società in generale. Credo nell'importanza della cittadinanza attiva. Faccio parte di un'associazione per la salvaguardia di un'isola della laguna. Poveglia, un'isola affascinante che stava per essere svenduta a un privato potrebbe domani diventare patrimonio della comunità e della sua socialità.
Oltre al lavoro qui con voi, lavoro come custode in alcuni palazzi dell'università di Venezia. Affitto questo appartamento a voi, miei cari futuri ospiti, per acquistare questo appartamento interamente. Questo è l'appartamento di famiglia, il luogo dove sono nata e ho speso la mia infanzia e adolescenza. Oggi sto acquistando la quota di mia sorella per diventarne la sola proprietaria. Vi ringrazio di cuore per quel che farete perché mi aiutate a coltivare le mie radici in questa isola speciale dove porterò avanti la mia famiglia. Grazie mille :))

name: Murano Suites | Rubino - Water view & Fireplace
description:
License IT027042C2RLMBGPBI

MURANO Suites - RUBINO, 70sqm of exclusivity. On the first floor, overlooking the Grand Canal of Murano with a striking view from a royal arched window that conveys the feeling of sleeping in the water.

Great brightness given by 4 dormers installed in the exposed wooden roof. In the center, a two-sided fireplace divides the sleeping area from the living area, a particular situation that is probably unique in its context.
neighborhood_overview:
We are on the Rivalonga, the bank of the Murano's Grand Canal. The sunniest shore and most central which allows you to reach Venice by vaporetto with a connection every 10 minutes during the day and every 20 minutes throughout the night.
Absolute Serenity with everything at your fingertips!

MURANO is one of the enchanting islands of the Venetian Lagoon, located north-east of the city and divided into seven small islands, each separated by canals and connected by bridges.

The Venetian navigation network guarantees an easy connection between Murano and Venice throughout the day and night, Marco Polo Airport and the other islands of the lagoon.

On Wednesday and Saturday mornings, a characteristic boat offers fresh products, vegetables, fruits and flowers from the island of Sant'Erasmo on the shore between the Ponte Longo and the MUSEO stop: "km0".
host_about:

All my properties are completely new, fresh and bright!

My MURANO Suites listing is a Boutique apart' hotel concept, here I created four independent apartments, each with different and unique features. One has a roof top terrace, one has a fireplace, one has a priceless panoramic view of the Murano Grand Canal and one has a sitting area and deck chairs on the terrace with view on the glass factories roofs.
 
Each apartment is unique on its own way with features that will really make you feel like a true Venetian.

On April 2019 I've added the MURANO Place brand to my listings, this is a selection of high level properties all over the island always selected with the most important features I consider : central location, easy access to public transportation to and from the airport and to and from the main Island of Venice but most of all, my apartments must offer a full immersion into the Venetian local people lifestyle.

During their stay, my guests are completely autonomous but I am just one phone call away for any assistance.

Reading my previous guests reviews, I think that you will love the Murano experience I offer.
Elodie

Inoltre avrete la comodità di accedere al bagno privato direttamente dalla vostra camera mentre nel corridoio esterno, illuminato a giorno da un caratteristico balconcino, si trova un piccolo cucinino con il lavello, il frigo, il forno a gas e il microonde.
Nella grande camera da letto ci sono due balconi che affacciano in un grande canale con gondole di passaggio e sopratutto di fronte all'antico Palazzo Mastelli nota meta turistica veneziana.
Vi auguro una buona permanenza nella Casa di San Martino a Venezia.

For your Holidays without troubles!! Let me introduce myself. I’m Manuela, I’m 35 years old and I was born in Venice. I love my city, I consider it unique but I know like every major tourist destination, Venice has two different faces. There’s the Venice of the tourists, made of predictable routes and their restaurants, created for those who are just passing by and probably are not coming back twice. You spend hours queued just to visit the most famous churches or museums. That’s the chaotic Venice, with a lot of unfamiliar faces that don’t give help when you need it. And then there is the Venice of the Venetians, where everybody knows each other. That’s the Venice with secret restaurants, bars and cicchetterie (typical Venetian local) where you can eat divinely without spending too much, places frequented by people who charachterise and make the city unique. That’s not the touristic Venice: even those who are visiting the city for the first time, can feel its real soul. And this is the Venice I’d like people to know, even if for just a few days. 
Therefore, if you don’t like the “tourist trap” city but you want to see its real soul, let me host you in my house. By booking a stay at Venetian MOOD, you won’t only choose a place to sleep, but you will be greeted by friends you can count on, in order to live your experience in Venice in the best way! Carefree, without stress or last minute bad surprises. If you’re looking to be a tourist in Venice, to eat in expensive low level restaurants and bars, to get carried away by the routes designed for tourists regardless of who they are, I respect that, but you might prefer another housing.

description:

neighborhood_overview:
Santa Maria Formosa, the campo (square) close to our B&B Aria e Luce, is one of the oldest in Venice, located here is the Querini Stampalia Foundation and of the marvellous church built by Jacopo Sansovino. We are located at the very beginning of Castello, the most “Venetian” sestiere (neighbourhood) of Venice, populated by many local residents, but just a few minutes’ walk from Piazza San Marco, Riva degli Schiavoni and Rialto.
In the area there are still many traditional workshops, typical bars and "osterie" (small restaurants), as well as many other services (vaporetto ferry stops, supermarkets, essential shops and the Civil Hospital too). You will be surrounded by Venetian art and architecture, but not overwhelmed by crowds of tourists!
host_about:
Siamo Luca e Arianna, una coppia quarantenne, con un bambino di cinque anni, Sebastiano.
Arianna è un architetto, che però ama fare un po' di tutto, molto socievole, le cui passioni sono leggere, l'arte e il teatro (ha recitato per tanti anni). Io, Luca, sono un barista, appassionato di fotografia, buona cucina e di viaggi (ho passato due anni in Australia e nel sud-est asiatico, visitando e lavorando). 
Entrambi amiamo tantissimo Venezia,  la nostra città che conosciamo molto bene al di fuori degli itinerari turistici e nei suoi aspetti meno noti: la sua architettura anche contemporanea, gli angoli più fotografici, i luoghi particolari, i locali speciali- 
Ci piace condividere le nostre conoscenze e le nostre scoperte e non vediamo l'ora di farlo.
Siamo tutti e due bravi cuochi e le serate migliori per noi sono quelle passate davanti a un'ottima cena, con un buon bicchiere di vino, a chiacchierare con vecchi e nuovi amici. 
Una delle cose che preferiamo è avere ospiti e condividere con altre persone che non amino la vacanza mordi e fuggi. Per noi una sistemazione accogliente dove stare, in qualsiasi posto del mondo, deve avere un suo carattere e uno "spirito", non dev'essere impersonale. Dobbiamo poterci sentire a casa e avere l'opportunità di conoscere veramente persone ed esperienze e modi di vivere, non solo monumenti e località. 
Tutto questo è ciò che vogliamo trasmettere a chi starà da noi.
E soprattutto desideriamo avere ed offrire un posto pulito e bello! Perché crediamo entrambi fermamente che la bellezza salverà il mondo :)
--------
We are Luca and Arianna, a couple on their fourties, and our family is made of a third member,our baby boy Sebastiano.
Arianna is an architect by trade but she loves to do a bit of everything and lives a social life. She is fond of reading, art and theatre (she acted for many years). Me, Luca, I'm a barman,  passionate about photography, good cooking and travelling (I spent almost two years in Australia and in Southeast Asia, visiting and working there).
We both love Venice, our city, which we know very well, outside of the common tourist way and in its less known features: its architecture, both historic and contemporary, secret corners that must be photographed, the peculiar places, the coolest bars and restaurants. 
We like to share what we know and what we are discovering and we cannot wait to do so!
We are both good cooks and for us the perfect night is one spent around a table, with an excellent meal and a good glass of wine, chatting with friends both new and old. 
One of the things that we love most is having guests and sharing with people who don’t just like a quick holiday getaway, but the real discover of people and places. To us a welcoming place to stay wherever around the world has to have a spine and a “soul”, it cannot be impersonal. We need to feel at home and have the chance to really know different people and experience the way of living, not just monuments and localities. That is what we would like to offer to my guests. Above all, we would like to offer a tidy and beautiful place! Because we deeply believe that beauty will save us all. :)

neighborhood_overview:
San Polo is the smallest of the six sestieri of Venice, along the Grand Canal. It is one of the oldest parts of the city, having been settled before the ninth century, when it and San Marco formed part of the Realtine Islands. The sestiere is named for the Church of San Polo.

The district has been the site of Venice's main market since 1097, and connected to the eastern bank of the Grande Canal by the Rialto bridge since the thirteenth century. The western part of the quarter is now known for its churches, while the eastern part, sometimes just called the Rialto, is known for its palaces and smaller houses.

Attractions in San Polo include the Rialto Bridge, the Church of San Giacomo di Rialto (according to legend the oldest in the city), the Campo San Polo with the Church of San Polo, the House of Goldoni, the Church of Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari, the Church of San Rocco and the Scuola Grande di San Rocco.

A beautifully furnished jewel of an apartment in a privileged position in the Cannaregio ‘sestiere’…

neighborhood_overview:
The Cannaregio Canal, which was the main route into the city until the construction of a railway link to the mainland, gave the district its name (Canal Regio is Italian for Royal Canal). Development began in the eleventh century as the area was drained and parallel canals were dredged. Although elegant palazzos were built facing the Grand Canal, the area grew primarily with working class housing and manufacturing. Beginning in 1516, Jews were restricted to living in the Venetian Ghetto. It was enclosed by guarded gates and no one was allowed to leave from sunset to dawn. However, Jews held successful positions in the city such as merchants, physicians, money lenders, and other trades. Restrictions on daily Jewish life continued for more than 270 years, until Napoleon Bonaparte conquered the Venetian Republic in 1797. He removed the gates and gave all residents the freedom to live where they chose.

host_about:
IO E VENEZIA
Nonostante vi ci abbia comprato casa, non posso certo sostenere di conoscere Venezia come le mie tasche: pur avendo una nonna nativa dell'Isola di Burano, non sono una veneziana, ma una torinese dal sangue misto terribilmente affascinata da una città a forma di pesce che trova le sue fondamenta nell'acqua salata del mare.
Trovarmi a Venezia priva di senso dell'orientamento non mi spaventa, anzi, mi invita ad iniziare a camminare, a smarrirmi tra le calli, scoprendo, ammirando, inseguendo quei dettagli che solo una città dalla storia millenaria può offrire. Archi a tutto sesto, mattoni a vista, bassorilievi, e poi altane, corti, pozzi, ponti, sottoporteghi, colori, profumi; non c'è un angolo che si ripeta, è tutto straordinariamente unico!
L'impronta bizantina dona alla città quel tocco di esotico che ti porta inevitabilmente a sognare, e l' espressione più immediata non può essere altro che "Meraviglioso!". Ma Venezia non è solo stupore; Venezia è curiosità, è tradizione, è "il veneziano"!
Dimenticatevi della tecnologia e passeggiate col naso all'insù. Noterete che ogni calle, al posto dei classici cartelli indicanti le vie, possiede il suo "Nizioleto", rigorosamente eseguito a mano e ribattuto nel momento in cui il salso e il tempo lo portano a perdere di brillantezza. Di alcuni di questi mi piace andarne a scoprire la toponomastica, talora piuttosto eloquente. Ad esempio, il "Ponte de le tette" pare abbia tale denominazione perché nei pressi di esso le meretrici comparivano sulle porte e alle finestre con i seni scoperti. Oppure "Campiello del Pestrin", ove, ai tempi della Serenissima, erano presenti i Pestrineri, gli artigiani che lavoravano il latte. E che dire di "Calle Stretta"?! Appena 65 cm di larghezza!
Insomma, è veramente impossibile non farsi rapire da tanta magnificenza e stravaganza, un cocktail perfetto che rende Venezia una delle città storiche più belle al mondo.
Potrei andare avanti per ore a raccontarvi un'infinità di belle storie, ma preferisco lasciarvi a disposizione la mia Casa e darvi modo di scoprirle direttamente, magari proprio come faccio io...perdendovi...disorientandovi...vagabondando...facendo della vostra meta l'emozione, la sensazione, l'ispirazione lasciata da ogni singolo passo.

VENICE AND ME
Despite the fact that I bought a house there, I can't say that I know Venice like the back of my hands: although my grandmother comes from the Isle of Burano, I don’t come from Venice, but I’m a mixed blood girl from Turin, terribly fascinated by a city shaped like a fish and built on the salt water of the sea.
Being in Venice without a sense of direction doesn't frighten me, in fact it invites me to start walking, to get lost in the streets, discovering, admiring, chasing those details that only a city with a millennial history can offer. Round arches, exposed bricks, bas-reliefs, and then altane, courtyards, shafts, bridges, sotoporteghi, colors, perfumes; every corner is different, everything is extremely unique!
The Byzantine style gives to the city that exotic touch that inevitably leads you to dream, and the most immediate expression can only be “Wonderful!”. But Venice is not only astonishment; Venice is curiosity, tradition, it‘s “the Venetian”!
Forget about technology and walk around with upturned noses. You will notice that each street, instead of classic signs indicating its name, has its "Nizioleto", rigorously handmade and reversed when the sauce and the time lead him to lose brilliance. I like discovering the toponimy of some of them, sometimes quite revealing. For example, the Ponte de le tette (“the bridge of the breasts”) seems to be called this way because of the whores appearing in front of the doors and the windows with their uncovered breast. Or Campiello del Pestrin, where at the time of the Serenissima there were the Pestrineri, the artisans working the milk. And what about Calle stretta (“narrow street”)? Just 65 cm wide!
Well, it’s really impossible not to be kidnapped by this magnificence and extravagance, a perfect mixture that makes Venice one of the most beautiful historical cities in the world.
I could continue like this for hours and keep telling you an infinity of beautiful stories, but I prefer to leave you my Home and give you the opportunity to discover them directly, maybe just like I do… losing yourself… bewildering… wandering…  allowing the emotion, the feeling, the inspiration left by each single step to become your destination.

host_about:
Sono Silvia, property manager e titolare dell’agenzia Immobiliare Veneziacentopercento, specializzata in ambito turistico nel centro storico di Venezia. 
Sono appassionata di arte, musica e Venezia, dove sono nata dove ho sempre vissuto. 
Nel 1995 ho unito i miei interessi per creare e costruire la mia attività, con l’obbiettivo di condividere con quante più persone possibile l'atmosfera di una città speciale e unica, diversa da qualsiasi altra  al mondo, facendola conoscere e amare nei suoi aspetti più intimi.
Ho iniziato con una sola stanza, a Casa mia, che ancora oggi è un B&B, fino a gestire oltre 20 diverse strutture per conto terzi.
Ho scelto di concentrarmi nel Sestiere di Castello, fulcro dell'antica Serenissima, perché qui è ancora possibile apprezzare appieno la più autentica quotidianità veneziana.
Per me e il mio staff la priorità assoluta è aiutare gli ospiti a vivere un’esperienza “al cento per cento”, cercando di trasformare i semplici turisti in viaggiatori consapevoli, “veneziani temporanei”, trasmettendo loro la passione per Venezia e il suo ambiente complesso e delicato, dove acqua e terra si sono unite come in una magia.

host_about:
I spent most part of my life studying nature, which is a big passion.
I like traveling whenever I can and knowing new people and other cultures is my must. That's why I decided to be a Airbnb host: is a way to travel without moving.
7 years ago, nearly as a joke, I started Venice Suites srls with a couple of friends.
We began with one apartment, and now we have 10 apartments and we would like to become bigger!
We would be very happy to show you the city and its surroundings, making you living the Venetian experience and tasting the differences from the other cities in the world. So, not only the greatest Saint Mark's square, but you will enjoy the cuisine, the Venetian sounds, the mainland and the lagoon. What do you think about skying in the Dolomites mountains(i.e. in Cortina) during the day, and sleeping in the historic center of Venice at the same time?
If you have imagination, the most part is done!

name: Sartor Apartment with Canal View and Private Court
description: Integrating chic Italian design with meticulously restored architectural details such as Venetian terrazzo flooring and colourful frescoes, these remarkable properties range from a well-proportioned studio with shared furnished courtyard, to a bright and beautiful 2 bedroom Piano Nobile apartment, each offering guests a unique opportunity to sample the joys of elegant palazzo living in one of the most authentic Venetian districts of town.
neighborhood_overview:
A trendsetting apartment harking back to days of old in a privileged position in the Cannaregio ‘sestiere’…
… A much-loved district with a traditional old-world charm characterised by peaceful residential areas, a host of historic landmarks including the spectacular fairy tale Ca’ d’Oro and the ancient Jewish Ghetto, plus long and wide canal-side ‘fondamente’ including the Fondamente de la Misericordia and de la Sensa (with their fabulous selection of local restaurants and ‘bacari’ – including our favourites Anice Stellato, Paradiso Perdutoand Vino Vero), and the Fondamente Nove – Venice’s northern waterfront overlooking the waters of the lagoon towards the distant peaks of the Dolomite mountains.

Within an easy stroll of some wonderful churches including the dainty jewel-box Santa Maria dei Miracoli, the Gesuiti with its towering white façade and statues of the Apostles, and Madonna dell’ Orto - final resting place of the painter Tintoretto who lived nearby.

My passions are: classic dance, handicrafts and cooking (especially sweets!).

host_about:
Sono Silvia, property manager e titolare dell’agenzia Immobiliare Veneziacentopercento, specializzata in ambito turistico nel centro storico di Venezia. 
Sono appassionata di arte, musica e Venezia, dove sono nata dove ho sempre vissuto. 
Nel 1995 ho unito i miei interessi per creare e costruire la mia attività, con l’obbiettivo di condividere con quante più persone possibile l'atmosfera di una città speciale e unica, diversa da qualsiasi altra  al mondo, facendola conoscere e amare nei suoi aspetti più intimi.
Ho iniziato con una sola stanza, a Casa mia, che ancora oggi è un B&B, fino a gestire oltre 20 diverse strutture per conto terzi.
Ho scelto di concentrarmi nel Sestiere di Castello, fulcro dell'antica Serenissima, perché qui è ancora possibile apprezzare appieno la più autentica quotidianità veneziana.
Per me e il mio staff la priorità assoluta è aiutare gli ospiti a vivere un’esperienza “al cento per cento”, cercando di trasformare i semplici turisti in viaggiatori consapevoli, “veneziani temporanei”, trasmettendo loro la passione per Venezia e il suo ambiente complesso e delicato, dove acqua e terra si sono unite come in una magia.

Castello is the most extensive of the six sestieri or districts of central Venice. It covers the long eastern part of the city - if Venice is a fish, then Castello is its tail. To the west it reaches into the heart of town, close to the Rialto. Eastwards it stretches past the Arsenale and Giardini Pubblici towards the leafy modern housing of Sant'Elena.

host_about:
"Fenix" è una società a gestione famigliare, siamo fratello e sorella, rispettivamente Matteo e Francesca.
Il nome della società con cui lavoriamo, Fenix, ha un duplice significato. Il primo legato alla "fenice", in quanto simbolo di ciclicità e di novità. Infatti, il settore turistico é un terreno a noi già noto che avevamo cominciato a praticare con nostro padre. Quando quest'ultimo ha deciso di ritirarsi abbiamo deciso di rinascere come "Fenix", creando un nuovo ambiente lavorativo, ma pur mantenendo invariata buona parte della gestione passata. 
Il secondo significato vuole richiamare allo storico "Gran Teatro La Fenice" di Venezia, dai cui titoli delle opere liriche abbiamo preso ispirazione per distinguere in modo originale e fantasioso i nomi delle nostre proprietà (Aida, Bohéme, Otello, Do Dogi, Colombina, Armida).
Lavoriamo con le locazioni turistiche a Venezia da ormai qualche anno, più precisamente nel sestiere (zona) di Castello, il quartier generale della famosa e storica Biennale di Venezia.
Siamo giovani ed intraprendenti, ci piace conoscere nuove persone ed offrire piacevoli soggiorni all'insegna della tipica vita veneziana.
Chi siamo?
Matteo: "Mi  piace molto l'attività fisica in generale, amo correre al Lido, piccola isola composta da un lembo di terra di 12km che offre spiagge e lunghe dighe sul mare da percorrere; studio economia qui a Venezia; amo la cucina veneziana con le sue ricche ricette a base di pesce;  il mio motto é "l'ozio è il padre dei vizi". "
Francesca: "oltre ad essere una lavoratrice, sono una giovane mamma a tempo pieno di due dolci bambine, Benedetta e Daniela; mi piace molto leggere libri; trascorro il tempo libero con il mio compagno e le mie figlie; amo viaggiare e vedere posti nuovi, specialmente se offrono un clima tropicale; il mio motto è "impara l'arte e mettila da parte". "
Entrambi apprezziamo stare in buona compagnia, specialmente se chi la offre conosce il rispetto e le buone maniere. 
Quando viaggiamo, ad entrambi piace instaurare relazioni con le persone che ci ospitano.
Infatti, dialogare con chi ospita non solo è sintomo di cordialità, ma normalmente garantisce di trascorrere un soggiorno migliore grazie a possibili consigli vantaggiosi ed alle opportunità che possono essere suggerite. 
Anche nelle vesti di host, possiamo definirci propensi ad instaurare rapporti durevoli con i clienti, pur rispettando gli spazi e la riservatezza di questi, ma rendendoci comunque sempre disponibili ad aiutarli con consigli per vivere Venezia al meglio e a soddisfare le loro necessità.

"Fenix" è una società a gestione famigliare, siamo fratello e sorella, rispettivamente Matteo e Francesca.

Chi siamo?
Matteo: "Mi  piace molto l'attività fisica in generale, amo correre al Lido, piccola isola composta da un lembo di terra di 12km che offre spiagge e lunghe dighe sul mare da percorrere; studio economia qui a Venezia; amo la cucina veneziana con le sue ricche ricette a base di pesce;  il mio motto é "l'ozio è il padre dei vizi". "

"
Entrambi apprezziamo stare in buona compagnia, specialmente se chi la offre conosce il rispetto e le buone maniere. 
Quando viaggiamo, ad entrambi piace instaurare relazioni con le persone che ci ospitano.
Infatti, dialogare con chi ospita non solo è sintomo di cordialità, ma normalmente garantisce di trascorrere un soggiorno migliore grazie a possibili consigli vantaggiosi ed alle opportunità che possono essere suggerite. 
Anche nelle vesti di host, possiamo definirci propensi ad instaurare rapporti durevoli con i clienti, pur rispettando gli spazi e la riservatezza di questi, ma rendendoci comunque sempre disponibili ad aiutarli con consigli per vivere Venezia al meglio e a soddisfare le loro necessità.

host_about:
"Fenix" è una società a gestione famigliare, siamo fratello e sorella, rispettivamente Matteo e Francesca.
Il nome della società con cui lavoriamo, Fenix, ha un duplice significato. Il primo legato alla "fenice", in quanto simbolo di ciclicità e di novità. Infatti, il settore turistico é un terreno a noi già noto che avevamo cominciato a praticare con nostro padre. Quando quest'ultimo ha deciso di ritirarsi abbiamo deciso di rinascere come "Fenix", creando un nuovo ambiente lavorativo, ma pur mantenendo invariata buona parte della gestione passata. 
Il secondo significato vuole richiamare allo storico "Gran Teatro La Fenice" di Venezia, dai cui titoli delle opere liriche abbiamo preso ispirazione per distinguere in modo originale e fantasioso i nomi delle nostre proprietà (Aida, Bohéme, Otello, Do Dogi, Colombina, Armida).
Lavoriamo con le locazioni turistiche a Venezia da ormai qualche anno, più precisamente nel sestiere (zona) di Castello, il quartier generale della famosa e storica Biennale di Venezia.
Siamo giovani ed intraprendenti, ci piace conoscere nuove persone ed offrire piacevoli soggiorni all'insegna della tipica vita veneziana.
Chi siamo?
Matteo: "Mi  piace molto l'attività fisica in generale, amo correre al Lido, piccola isola composta da un lembo di terra di 12km che offre spiagge e lunghe dighe sul mare da percorrere; studio economia qui a Venezia; amo la cucina veneziana con le sue ricche ricette a base di pesce;  il mio motto é "l'ozio è il padre dei vizi". "
Francesca: "oltre ad essere una lavoratrice, sono una giovane mamma a tempo pieno di due dolci bambine, Benedetta e Daniela; mi piace molto leggere libri; trascorro il tempo libero con il mio compagno e le mie figlie; amo viaggiare e vedere posti nuovi, specialmente se offrono un clima tropicale; il mio motto è "impara l'arte e mettila da parte". "
Entrambi apprezziamo stare in buona compagnia, specialmente se chi la offre conosce il rispetto e le buone maniere. 
Quando viaggiamo, ad entrambi piace instaurare relazioni con le persone che ci ospitano.
Infatti, dialogare con chi ospita non solo è sintomo di cordialità, ma normalmente garantisce di trascorrere un soggiorno migliore grazie a possibili consigli vantaggiosi ed alle opportunità che possono essere suggerite. 
Anche nelle vesti di host, possiamo definirci propensi ad instaurare rapporti durevoli con i clienti, pur rispettando gli spazi e la riservatezza di questi, ma rendendoci comunque sempre disponibili ad aiutarli con consigli per vivere Venezia al meglio e a soddisfare le loro necessità.

Palazzo Foscari (Cà Foscari, the main headquarters of the University of Cà Foscari where the offices and a new museum complex that close at 7.00 pm) and Palazzo Brandolini D’Adda. In the campiello there are not even benches where people can sit down, and the only shops that face the square are two bookstores, an antique shop and a fabric store, and all of them close at 7.00 pm. There are no bars or nightclubs even nearby, which attract noisy youth in the evening.

name: Venice's Heart
description: What makes this apartment unique is the location: overlooking a typical canal on one side and on the other on a street. The setting is typical Venetian, Castello, the largest district in the city. Classic "cicchetterie" and restaurants where you can taste typical Venetian dishes surround it. A few steps from the apartment, the Biennale garden stop from which the various lines that connect the whole city depart. 15 min walk separate you from the beautiful St. Mark's Square.
neighborhood_overview:
The Castello district is the greenest area in Venice considering the Gardens and the island of Sant'Elena with its extended pine forests, an ideal place to relax on a lawn with a nice book, admiring the lagoon and the City.
Also, not to be missed, a visit to discover the famous Arsenal and the Venice Biennale (a cultural institution that organizes the Venice Film Festival).
In Venice there is only one Via: Via Garibaldi. Take advantage of an Venetian experience by eating in the typical places, or buy fruits or vegetables from a boat.
Finally, don't miss the AcquaAlta Library, you'll be incredibly fascinated by the arrangement of books in places like boats, gondolas to save them in case of high water.
host_about:

name: Rio di San Barnaba Flat in Dorsoduro
description:
A great stylish apartment placed in one of most charming locations in Venice, in the heart of Dorsoduro.
Rio San Barnaba Flat overlooks one of the prettiest canals in all Venice, right next door to the Carmini Church and on the edge of S. Margherita square. neighborhood_overview:
ABOUT THE AREA:
Dorsoduro, is according to many, the most beautiful and interesting area in Venice.
With its Art Colleges and University, it has long been home to artists, designers, writers and educators.
In 1750, the Gallerie dell'Accademia first opened as an art school.
Peggy Guggenheim, the American heiress and art patron, settled in the Palazzo Venier dei Leoni in 1949. Nicknamed Il Palazzo Non Finito, this low-slung building is an unfinished palace dating to 1750.

The flat is a very short walk from the Accademia bridge (leading over the Grand Canal to Campo Santo Stefano) and it’s picture galleries (gallerie dell’Accademia), from the enchanting Zattere waterfront, La Salute Church, Punta della Dogana.
Very close by you can take a look at the Squero San Trovaso which was founded in the 17th Century and is one of very few working gondola boatyards left in Venice today, where local artisans continue to maintain and repair gondolas by hand.

Mestre is the mainland, modern part of Venice.

After a long day walking around tourist Venice, this is a great place to relax and reload your batteries.

neighborhood_overview: Cinqueteste Luxury Home is located in the Santa Croce district, along the Rio delle Muneghette where it is reflected in the water and front of Fondamenta de le Sechere. It is considered one of the most curious and photographed houses in Venice. Casa delle Cinque Teste (literally translated with House of the Five Heads) is the name given to it by the Venetians, but probably not the official one. The meaning of the five heads is due to five marble heads carved by the town's tagiapiera (or stonemasons) and representing gentle human faces placed on the facade of the building facing the water. Preciosity can be found also in the keystones, that together with the oval heads and windows, give unusual harmony to the front. Simple houses usually could not boast so many decorations, commonly reserved for noble’s buildings. Rio delle Muneghette is one of the longest and most tortuous canals in Venice, in fact, it starts from Campo Castelforte at the Scuola Grande di San Rocco and ends in Rio Mari

description:
Get the best of both worlds - live like a local and reach the biggest attractions within minutes in this newly renovated Venetian apartment.

The apartment is located in one of the most authentic areas of Venice, a unique area filled with locals, not tourists, creating a truly priceless atmosphere.

You’ll find everything you need no more than a few minutes from the apartment: an authentic bakery, two pizzerias, a cafe and tobacco shop are all less than 50 metres from the door.

neighborhood_overview: Dorsoduro is the brightest area of Venice. Strategically positioned between the two most prestigious cultural attractions: the “Gallerie dell’Accademia” with many paintings of major Venetian artists and the Peggy Guggenheim collection (inside Venier Palace on the “Canal Grande”). Moreover, there is the Contemporary Art Museum on “Punta della Dogana”, including the famous Pinault collection, and “Ca’ Rezzonico” an historical Venetian palace hosting the Museum of the 18th century. All these attractions are reachable walking few minutes. One can also stroll on Zattere bank admiring the huge “Canale della Giudecca” (Giudecca’s canal) and taste the “spritz”, a bubbling alcoholic aperitif prepared with Aperol (bitter liquor) and prosecco wine, or a tasteful gelato. Especially in Spring and Summer the bank is one of the favorite places for a walk. Dorsoduro is the ideal place to avoid crowded areas and enjoy the most beautiful and fascinating corners and squares of Venice

neighborhood_overview:
The Cannaregio district is the largest district in Venice and also the most populated. It is crossed by the Cannaregio Canal, the only one of the historic center that, together with the Grand Canal, is crossed by vaporetto.
The name of the district is presumed to derive either from the presence in the past of vast reeds (land cultivated with common reed) before the area was reclaimed and then inhabited, or from the name that had the canal that crossed it, namely Canal Regio, which connects the lagoon to the Grand Canal.
The Cannaregio district can be reached by line 4.1 and 5.1 of the vaporetto or by line 1, all lines that cross the Grand Canal and the Cannaregio Canal.
It's probably easier to walk from Venice Santa Lucia Station as it takes about ten minutes. You must leave the station behind you and head to the left, taking the foundation of the Scalzi and then take the Rio Terà List of Spain. You'll find yourself in the middle of the Cannaregio district.

host_about:
"Fenix" è una società a gestione famigliare, siamo fratello e sorella, rispettivamente Matteo e Francesca.
Il nome della società con cui lavoriamo, Fenix, ha un duplice significato. Il primo legato alla "fenice", in quanto simbolo di ciclicità e di novità. Infatti, il settore turistico é un terreno a noi già noto che avevamo cominciato a praticare con nostro padre. Quando quest'ultimo ha deciso di ritirarsi abbiamo deciso di rinascere come "Fenix", creando un nuovo ambiente lavorativo, ma pur mantenendo invariata buona parte della gestione passata. 
Il secondo significato vuole richiamare allo storico "Gran Teatro La Fenice" di Venezia, dai cui titoli delle opere liriche abbiamo preso ispirazione per distinguere in modo originale e fantasioso i nomi delle nostre proprietà (Aida, Bohéme, Otello, Do Dogi, Colombina, Armida).
Lavoriamo con le locazioni turistiche a Venezia da ormai qualche anno, più precisamente nel sestiere (zona) di Castello, il quartier generale della famosa e storica Biennale di Venezia.
Siamo giovani ed intraprendenti, ci piace conoscere nuove persone ed offrire piacevoli soggiorni all'insegna della tipica vita veneziana.
Chi siamo?
Matteo: "Mi  piace molto l'attività fisica in generale, amo correre al Lido, piccola isola composta da un lembo di terra di 12km che offre spiagge e lunghe dighe sul mare da percorrere; studio economia qui a Venezia; amo la cucina veneziana con le sue ricche ricette a base di pesce;  il mio motto é "l'ozio è il padre dei vizi". "
Francesca: "oltre ad essere una lavoratrice, sono una giovane mamma a tempo pieno di due dolci bambine, Benedetta e Daniela; mi piace molto leggere libri; trascorro il tempo libero con il mio compagno e le mie figlie; amo viaggiare e vedere posti nuovi, specialmente se offrono un clima tropicale; il mio motto è "impara l'arte e mettila da parte". "
Entrambi apprezziamo stare in buona compagnia, specialmente se chi la offre conosce il rispetto e le buone maniere. 
Quando viaggiamo, ad entrambi piace instaurare relazioni con le persone che ci ospitano.
Infatti, dialogare con chi ospita non solo è sintomo di cordialità, ma normalmente garantisce di trascorrere un soggiorno migliore grazie a possibili consigli vantaggiosi ed alle opportunità che possono essere suggerite. 
Anche nelle vesti di host, possiamo definirci propensi ad instaurare rapporti durevoli con i clienti, pur rispettando gli spazi e la riservatezza di questi, ma rendendoci comunque sempre disponibili ad aiutarli con consigli per vivere Venezia al meglio e a soddisfare le loro necessità.

name: Luxury Campo Santa Maria Formosa
description:
A stone's throw from Rialto and San Marco, inside the Campo Santa Maria Formosa, in a magical place where art, modernity and ancient everyday life of a Venice that is still itself coexist.

neighborhood_overview: In Campo Santa Maria Formosa you can choose to be inside the noise of the world, inside modernity and turning from the opposite side into the ancient silence of a Venice that although not rich in important monuments is still itself, not attacked by tourists; a Venice that leaves time for dialogue, that has time to talk with the tourist, still appreciated and treated as an opportunity to know different worlds and cultures,  with the same attitude that the merchant of the Serenissima of the 1400s had when sailing through the Mediterranean he met and reported stories and objects from distant worlds. Venice is a city that puts you to the test in the discomfort, in the climate, in the maze within which streets, squares and canals arise, but which then return all the effort you made by gifting you with wonder and a fullness of beauty unique in the world.

L'amore verso la cultura in generale e la cultura dell'ospitalità  è ciò che si potrà portare indietro, come regalo unico, nella propria valigia.

5 cose che mi piacciono? Vediamo...  Mi piace la diversità: cogliere le piccole cose che contraddistionguono ognuno di noi. Sono una persona che osserva molto, non per giudicare, bensì per apprendere dagli altri!  Mi piace conoscere il prossimo e le differenze che lo caratteristicano. 
Adoro la musica in tutte le sue forme e non faccio nulla senza. 
Sono legato ai miei fratelli in un modo speciale. E stare con loro è sicuramente una delle cose che mi piace di più. 
Ho l'istinto morboso di voler sempre essere al centro dell'attenzione con i miei amici, ma solamente per farli ridere. Adoro ridere e far ridere i miei amici, con i quali ho un legame indissolubile,  e li considero al pari dei miei fratelli!
Sono uno Scout, anche se in questo momento non ho più la possibilità di fare il capo, ma sicuramente lo scoutismo ha modellato il mio stile di vita in modo permanente. Educare bambini e ragazzi stando in mezzo a loro è la cosa più bella che ci sia in questo mondo.
Mi piace cantare, anche se non ho tante occasioni per farlo. Adoro i videogames, e spero un giorno di lavorare nell'ambito.  Il mio sogno sarebbe aprire un internet cafè, magari insieme ai miei fratelli!

Come accolgo gli ospiti? Nel modo più semplice possibile, con un sorriso! Sembrerà stupido, ma non c'è modo migliore di iniziare un rapporto. Cerco di essere il più disponibile possibile, ponendo il mio onore nel meritare fiducia.
